families.name: What the routines make reaches home
families.why: The morning Jobs run and the reflections routine put their files in the mailbox; home reads them every 15 minutes and keeps a checked copy, which is what the phone shows.

objectives.claim: When a mailbox pass goes wrong in more than one place, each one is reported.
objectives.requirement: When independent phases of one pass fail (inbound, filing, outbound, asks, archive), the log names each failed phase and its failure, and mailbox_poll_failing sets each distinct failure class; what the pass did keep is kept. Within the inbound phase, the folders after a failing one wait for the next pass.
objectives.conclusion: The log now names every phase that failed, not only the first. The dashboard's failing panel shows each kind of failure, not which phase it came from, and the test shows two phases failing together.

evidence.says: A pass with both its read and its hand-over failing reports both phases, in order, and counts their one class once.
mailbox_poll_failing is labelled by failure class, not by phase, so the panel cannot say which phase failed; the log line does.
Before server#527, the phases were joined with Result::and, so only the first failure reached the log and the metric.

objectives.claim: A poller that has stopped reads as stopped, not as quiet.
objectives.requirement: The poller stamps the start of every pass, so a dashboard can tell 'nothing new' (a recent stamp) from 'not running' (an old one), and 'switched off' from both.
objectives.conclusion: The dashboard reads a stale pass stamp as red while home's server is up; if the server itself is down it shows no data rather than red, and no test holds either.

evidence.says: mailbox_poll_last_attempt_timestamp_seconds moves when a pass starts; mailbox_poll_enabled says whether it should; the SINCE LAST READ panel turns red past two intervals.
The metric contract check only shows the dashboard reads a metric the server emits, not when it moves or what the panel does with it.

objectives.claim: If the poller stops, you are told within 18 minutes.
objectives.requirement: An alert fires when no pass has started within the interval plus the pass budget plus 60 seconds (900 + 120 + 60 at today's settings), and when the metric itself is missing; its delivery to the owner is tested.
objectives.conclusion: Nothing tells you: Prometheus has no alert rules, and the one provisioned Grafana alert is about logged errors.

evidence.says: rule_files is commented out in prometheus.yml.
The only provisioned alert counts tracing error events.

objectives.claim: A file put in the mailbox is at home within 20 minutes while home is up, or it shows as late.
objectives.requirement: From the Worker's commit to home's verified copy takes at most 20 minutes while home is available and the backlog is within one pass; past that, the oldest file still waiting is visible with its age, and time home was down is shown apart.
objectives.conclusion: Nothing measures how long a file waits, so whether this holds is unknown.

evidence.says: No metric records the age of the oldest file the mailbox holds that home has not kept.

objectives.claim: A whole mailbox pass has a time limit and a request limit.
objectives.requirement: One pass ends within 120 seconds and a shared request budget, with each phase keeping a reserve; what it could not do is deferred to the next pass and recorded.
objectives.conclusion: Each request has a 30-second limit but the pass has none: at today's constants a full pass may make up to 668 calls, about 5.5 hours of waiting in the worst case.

evidence.says: Inbound 4 × (10 pages + 20 gets) = 120, outbound 20, restore 8 × (1 + 50) = 408, archive 120: 668 calls, × 30 s ≈ 20,040 s.

objectives.claim: When there is nothing to do, the poller's own work stays small and counted.
objectives.requirement: With no files and no asks, a day of passes makes at most 384 mailbox requests without archiving and 1,920 with it; a change that raises either needs an amendment.
objectives.conclusion: The idle floor is known by arithmetic, not counted: no test runs a quiet day and counts the requests.

evidence.says: 96 passes a day × 4 folder listings = 384; with archiving, + 8 wanted listings + 8 archive listings = 20 a pass, 1,920 a day.

objectives.claim: The mailbox's database work is counted in D1's own numbers, per operation.
objectives.requirement: Each Worker operation totals D1's rows read and rows written from the statements it ran, and those totals are observable without any file's name or bytes.
objectives.conclusion: D1 returns its row counts with every statement, and the Worker throws them away.

evidence.says: The store's Db and Bound seam exposes rows and results only; d1Store drops meta.

families.name: Archived material can be asked for again
families.why: Home archives what has sat in the mailbox for a while; a routine that needs an old file asks for it, and home puts it back.

objectives.claim: Finding what the routine asked for costs the same however many asks are waiting.
objectives.requirement: Listing the oldest open asks in a folder reads in proportion to the page it returns, not to every ask in the folder.
objectives.conclusion: Measured locally: the work grows tenfold with each tenfold backlog, and an index makes it flat. D1's own row counts are not measured yet.

evidence.says: On the real migrations, the same 50 rows cost 12,066, 120,066 and 1,200,066 SQLite VM steps at 1k, 10k and 100k asks; 312 each with an index on (folder, asked_at, name). The query plan sorts every ask in a temporary B-tree.
D1 bills rows read, not VM steps, and the index adds a write and storage per ask; neither is measured on D1.

comparison.what: SQLite VM steps to list the 50 oldest open asks in one folder, local SQLite 3.53.1, same result rows
comparison.limits: Local SQLite steps, not D1's billed rows; excludes the index's extra write and storage per ask.

families.name: A request the app makes stops when you stop it
families.why: The shared fetch client carries the app's reads of lessons, word lists and the NFL data; a request it keeps making after you have moved on is work for nothing.

objectives.claim: A request stops when its caller cancels it, and 'no retries' means one try.
objectives.requirement: A call makes at most 1 + its own retry count attempts; once the caller's signal aborts, no attempt starts, a waiting backoff ends, and the call rejects as cancelled, never as timed out.
objectives.conclusion: Each way a cancel can arrive is tested, and zero retries makes one attempt. The app's query hooks do not pass React's cancel along yet (some-ui#2207).

evidence.says: Before #2202, an already-cancelled call still went out, a cancel mid-flight reached nothing, and retry count 0 made 2 attempts.

families.name: Voice notes sent home get heard
families.why: The phone sends a voice note home; home transcribes it in the background, and the transcript is what the routine reads.

objectives.claim: Every voice note sent home gets a transcript or a recorded reason it has none.
objectives.requirement: Each note home holds gets a row; a failed hearing is recorded and tried again on at most ATTEMPTS (3) passes, then stays recorded as failed, so no note is left without an outcome after three passes.
objectives.conclusion: Every note gets a row, and a failure is retried a few times and then kept as failed.

evidence.says: A pass gives every note a row and retries a failure a few times.

objectives.claim: A transcription pass takes a bounded batch.
objectives.requirement: One pass hears at most BATCH notes, each within its own deadline; the rest wait for the next pass.
objectives.conclusion: A pass hears at most a batch, and the next pass takes the rest.

evidence.says: A pass over more than a batch hears exactly a batch.

families.name: Study nudges stay bounded
families.why: Home decides when to nudge you to study from the phone's presence and signals, and sends the nudge by push.

objectives.claim: A nudge pass ends on time, and what it did not reach waits for the next one.
objectives.requirement: A waker pass reads at most BATCH due subjects and stops at its pass deadline; a subject it never reached is left untouched and still due.
objectives.conclusion: Held by the waker's written scaling rules and their tests: a bounded batch, one deadline, nothing lost at the cut.

evidence.says: A pass that reaches its deadline leaves the subjects it never reached untouched and still due; subjects beyond a batch are finished by later passes.
The scaling rules are written down: O(1) work per signal, an indexed range read, every pass bounded by BATCH and the deadline alone.

objectives.claim: If the nudge waker stops, you are told.
objectives.requirement: An alert fires when no waker pass has started within its interval plus its pass deadline plus 60 seconds, and when its metrics are missing; its delivery is tested.
objectives.conclusion: The dashboard shows when the waker last ran; nothing tells you when it stops.

evidence.says: nudge_waker_last_attempt_timestamp_seconds exists, and no alert rule reads it.

families.name: The morning run leaves an outcome
families.why: The 7:52 Jobs routine runs off home, at Anthropic; a run that never starts leaves nothing behind unless something expects it.

objectives.claim: A morning run that never started shows as missing when you open Jobs, not as a quiet morning.
objectives.requirement: When the run is due and home keeps run records but holds none for today, Today says home has no record of a run, apart from a run that found nothing.
objectives.conclusion: Jobs tells a missing run apart from an empty one, once you open it.

evidence.says: Today says home has no record of a run, only from a home that keeps them.

proof: some-ui:apps/www/src/lib/jobs/__tests__/morning.test.ts#says home has no record of a run only from a home that keeps them

objectives.claim: If the morning run has not happened 30 minutes after it was due, you are told.
objectives.requirement: Home expects each scheduled run by its time zone's clock, and an alert fires when none is recorded 30 minutes after it was due; its delivery is tested.
objectives.conclusion: Nothing on home expects the run, so a missed run is noticed only when you open Jobs.

evidence.says: Run records are written by the run itself; no schedule on home says when one is owed.

families.name: The checks themselves
families.why: Every promise above is only as good as the checks that hold it and what happens when one fails.

objectives.claim: A failing check stops a merge, in both repositories.
objectives.requirement: main in some-ui requires CI Gate, and main in the server requires one gate that waits on every check; a deliberately failing pull request is shown to be blocked in each.
objectives.conclusion: Last read on 2026-10-26, main was unprotected in both repositories, so a red check informs but cannot stop a merge.

evidence.says: GET /repos/paulgsc/{some-ui,server}/branches/main returned protected: false, and each repository's one ruleset had enforcement disabled (recon, 2026-10-26).

objectives.claim: Every route the server serves is accounted for here.
objectives.requirement: Every module in the server's route snapshot is in exactly one family or in the synchronous list, with a reason; a new module fails the check until someone places it.
objectives.conclusion: check:assurance fails a server module that is in no family and not listed as synchronous.

evidence.says: The coverage rule's test fails an unplaced and a stale module.

objectives.claim: Loosening what a promise requires shows, with who decided it.
objectives.requirement: Against the base branch, an objective is never removed, and each of these needs a new amendment linking the owner's decision: a holds that stops holding, a changed claim, requirement, kind or property, a weaker watch, a loosened or dropped bound, a retirement. A route module leaving a family for synchronous needs a decision too.
objectives.conclusion: check:assurance fails each of those without an amendment, and the amendment shows on this page. Whether a conclusion's wording still matches its evidence, and whether a proof really reaches its requirement, are left to review.

evidence.says: The ratchet's tests fail each of those changes without an amendment and pass it with one; a conclusion rewritten or a proof swapped is not among them.

objectives.claim: The server's own checks hold its half of this ledger.
objectives.requirement: Server CI reads this ledger, fails when a server path a holds names is missing, and fails a background task that belongs to no family.
objectives.conclusion: Nothing in the server reads this ledger yet, so a renamed server test would leave a proof here pointing at nothing.

evidence.says: check:assurance checks only some-ui paths; a server path is taken as written, and nothing in the server reads this ledger.
